name: NYU Marron Institute of Urban Management
recommendations_evidence: "Eye in the Sky: Harnessing AI to Monitor Police Response to Illegal Parking Complaints" (2025-08-22) abstract: "The results strengthen the case for increased automated ticketing systems, enhanced police oversight, and street designs that inherently discourage such violations." Also "A Better Billion: Expanding Transit & Housing for a More Affordable New York" (2026-03-19), which proposes 41 miles of subway extensions across 12 projects and estimates 167,064 new housing units around 64 new stations.
volume_note: Exact count of items on /papers dated on or after 2025-01-01, enumerated by walking the offset pagination: The Skyscraper Revolution (2026-03-09), A Blueprint for Successful Family-Based Diversion Programs (2025-08-22), Eye in the Sky (2025-08-22), The Essential Role of Air Quality Monitoring at U.S. Embassies and Consulates (2025-08-22), community health worker intervention among Denotified Tribes (2025-05-01), Estimating Reporting Bias in 311 Complaint Data (2025-03-21), Labor Trafficking in Construction and Hospitality Topical Brief (2025-03-21), Understanding the Needs of Unstably Housed Youth in New York City (2025-02-24). The next item back is dated 2024-12-17, confirming the cutoff. Roughly half are NYC-specific. The separate /blog stream carries 100+ additional items over the same period, of which 11 of 100 have NYC in the title.
verdict_reason: Publishes papers and reports making explicit recommendations to New York City agencies on policing, parking enforcement, transit expansion and 311 data, though a substantial share of its output is global rather than NYC.
note: Fetch is set to html rather than rss on purpose. The RSS feed at /feed is a valid RSS 2.0 document but carries NO <pubDate> element at all; dates appear only in <dc:date>, and those are batched newsletter-publication dates (12 distinct dates across 100 items), not true per-item publication dates. Use the feed for change detection only and take real dates from the HTML listing. The feed mixes blog posts and papers (7 of 100 items link to /papers/) and is capped at 100 items, oldest entry 2025-03-21. Not WordPress: /wp-json/wp/v2/posts returns 404, as do /papers/feed, /rss and /blog/feed. Papers pagination is offset-based (/papers, /papers/P3, /papers/P6 ... last page /papers/P138, step 3); a ?page=N query string is ignored and silently returns page 1, which will produce false duplicate counts if used. The /press listing is media coverage of Marron work, not testimony, so it should not be treated as a publication stream.

name: Sam Schwartz Transportation Research Program, Roosevelt House Public Policy Institute at Hunter College
recommendations_evidence: "How Would For-Hire Autonomous Vehicles Impact New York City? Lessons from California on Safety, VMT, and Parking" (July 2026) makes seven explicit recommendations to the city, including "Require robotaxi companies to compare their safety data to professional, for-hire vehicle drivers as a prerequisite to licensure to operate" and "Consider limiting robotaxis' ability to travel within dense, transit-rich commercial areas."
volume_note: Exact count. The reports page lists exactly two items, both after 2025-01-01. (1) "Congestion Pricing One Year Later" (January 2026), with the Regional Plan Association, hosted at https://rpa.org/news/lab/congestion-pricing-one-year-later. This one is a documentary data index and does NOT make explicit recommendations. (2) "How Would For-Hire Autonomous Vehicles Impact New York City?" (July 2026), with Open Plans, hosted at https://www.openplans.org/how-for-hire-autonomous-vehicles-impact-nyc. This one does make seven explicit recommendations. So two reports, one of which carries recommendations.
verdict_reason: Verified to exist, is entirely focused on New York City transportation policy and its most recent report makes seven explicit recommendations to city government, but total output is very low at two reports.
note: NAME CORRECTION: it is the Sam Schwartz Transportation Research PROGRAM (SSTRP), not a "Center" and not a "Transportation Research Center". It is housed at the Roosevelt House Public Policy Institute at Hunter College, CUNY, launched September 2025 with a $1M gift from Sam Schwartz. Chair: Sam Schwartz; Director: Kelly McGuinness. The reports page is a static WordPress page with no machine-readable dates: dates appear only as parenthetical text such as "(July 2026)", so the entry text must be parsed. Roosevelt House DOES have a working RSS feed (https://www.roosevelthouse.hunter.cuny.edu/feed/, 25 items, valid pubDate) and a working /wp-json/wp/v2/posts endpoint, but NEITHER surfaces the SSTRP reports; both carry general Roosevelt House institutional news only. That is why feed_url is null for this publisher. Both reports are hosted on partner sites (RPA, Open Plans), not on the Hunter domain, so the tracker must follow outbound links. The /press subpage is a long list of media hits and op-eds by Schwartz and McGuinness (Streetsblog, Gothamist, Daily News, Crain's, NYT) and is heavily oriented to New York City government, but it is commentary rather than qualifying publications.

name: NYU Furman Center for Real Estate and Urban Policy
recommendations_evidence: "The House Doesn't Always Win: Understanding NYC's Housing Connect Lottery System and How to Improve It" (2026-04-02) and "What the Charter Revision Commission's Ballot Proposals May Mean for New York City's Housing Production" (2025-10-15) are both directed at city housing policy. Note that much of the Furman corpus is empirical rather than prescriptive, so per-item screening is still required.
volume_note: Exact count from the X-WP-Total response header on https://www.furmancenter.org/wp-json/wp/v2/publication?per_page=100&after=2025-01-01T00:00:00, which returned x-wp-total: 31 and x-wp-totalpages: 1. Not all 31 make explicit recommendations.
verdict_reason: Primary New York City focus and high volume, but a large share of output is empirical housing research that does not make explicit recommendations, so items must be screened individually rather than included wholesale.
note: CONFIRMED LISTING URL, which corrects the entry in publishers_known.json. https://furmancenter.org/research does NOT resolve to a listing; it 301-redirects to an individual publication page. The real listing is https://www.furmancenter.org/publications/ (note the www and the trailing slash). Best fetch method is the WordPress REST API custom post type: /wp-json/wp/v2/publication, which supports after=, orderby=date and per_page= and exposes X-WP-Total for exact counting. The default /wp-json/wp/v2/posts endpoint returns an empty array, and the RSS feed at /feed/ is a valid but ITEM-LESS document (channel metadata only, zero <item> elements), so neither is usable. Other potentially useful custom post types on the same API: soc-report (State of the City), news, media-mention, data-tool, enacted-legislation. This record supersedes the furman entry in publishers_known.json, which lists an incorrect listing_url and fetch method.
